newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- DEC 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- DEC 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--With losses to the economy increasing daily and farmers apparently determined to stay put at their road blocks at least until the start Monday of Parliament's discussion of the budget, the government is looking to judicial and local bodies to exert pressure on the farmers. Meanwhile, a number of road blocks in Macedonia and Thrace were dismantled yesterday.
--The latest quarterly report from the Foundation of Industrial and Economic Research (IOBE) says that the government's mix of economic policies is not potent enough to push inflation down further.

--Despite the government's insistence that it will not meet economic demands, certain sectors are continuing to protest, with doctors at state hospitals and state school teachers in their second day of strike action. Participation is estimated at over 70 percent. Construction workers join them today.

--Athens is optimistic that tomorrow's EU summit in Dublin will for the first time adopt Greek positions on the security of the Union's external borders. However, a strike by diplomatic staff means the Greek delegation will be without support in Dublin.
--Greece and Cyprus decided on further joint military exercises during the coming year at a meeting yesterday between the countries' defence ministers.

--As the Greek Aris and Turkish Besiktas basketball teams brawled at their Korac Cup match in Thessaloniki last night, Olympic weightlifting medallists Valerios Leonidas and Naim Suleymanoglou presented a model of Greek-Turkish friendship, visiting a young car accident victim.

--The government said yesterday it would re-evaluate losses suffered by cotton producers and lead the battle at Brussels for more subsidies, in an effort to budge the farmers from their positions on the country's main roads.

--Dimitri Liani-Papandreou's interview with 'Paris Match' sets tongues wagging about whether she will run for public office. Liani-Papandreou says she "fell in love with politics" after living with Andreas Papandreou, the late prime minister and founder of ruling party PASOK.

--The opposition and government clashed over the farmers' blockade yesterday as conservative opposition leader Miltiades Evert visited with farmers at their road blocks. The government's spokesman accused Evert and other opposition leaders planning visits of irresponsibility. ETHNOS

--A distinguished academic says he has evidence that Turkey resorted to international courts over the sovereignty of the Dodecanese islands in 1929 and then withdrawn its claim following the 1932 treaty with Italy.

--New Democracy leader Evert's initiative to meet with all political party leaders and the prime minister on Monday could lead to the solution of the farmers' blockade. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
